success_patterns: Six of the eight clues were reproduced nearly word for word in a trivia-archive line, or in a phrase repeated across many passages (Seer of Seers, Creed/Scream, Bridge to Terabithia). The agent copied the entity attached to that phrase instead of reasoning from its own knowledge.

Type fit was honored. 'this country' gave the country (Zimbabwe), not the town in the clue. 'this film series' gave the series base name (Scream), not the installment (Scream 3) that dominated the passages. 'these ... animals' gave the plural (Crabs). 'this novel' gave the title with 'The' kept (The Outsiders).

Clue-stated parts were stripped and the missing part given alone ('Bridge to' -> Terabithia). A holiday name kept its head word when the bare modifier would not name it (Valentine's Day, not Valentine's).
The final answers were bare, short, and in the passages' own form, with no descriptor or explanation inside the answer tags.

patch.reasoning: Most successes were already covered by Rule 3 (verbatim archive hit) and the type and form rules. Prior epochs show that large mandatory-template rewrites regressed scores badly (0.735 down to 0.38-0.69), so no top-level restructuring is proposed. Two successes show a gap worth reinforcing: (a) series or franchise clues, where passages are full of one specific installment and the answer is the series name, and (b) holiday or event names, where the generic word is part of the proper name. Both are narrow, keyed to visible clue features, and unlikely to hurt stable passes.

edits.target: - 'One of these <role/title>' ('the 14th one of these spiritual leaders') asks for the title or category noun itself (Dalai Lama), not the individual named in the clue.
edits.content: - 'This film series / franchise / TV series / book series' asks for the SERIES base name, not one installment, sequel number or subtitle that the passages happen to dwell on ('Scream', not 'Scream 3'). Use the name shared by all the installments the passages mention. A clue that says 'this film' or 'this novel' (singular, one work) wants that single title with its leading 'The' kept if it is part of the title ('The Outsiders').

edits.target: The same holds for named events, deals, treaties, wars and laws when the clue gives only a generic descriptor with the head word ('1853 purchase that brought the U.S. to its present area' -> 'Gadsden Purchase', not 'Gadsden').
edits.content: The same holds for holidays and observances: 'this holiday' -> "Valentine's Day" (a bare "Valentine's" or 'Valentine' is not the holiday's name), 'Groundhog Day', 'Labor Day'. Copy the holiday's full standard name as the passages write it.
